conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (e.g. the local commit dbc297110af3b223acc81e203191c0a3bcd956b7: "feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)"); every commit GPG-signed and DCO signed off: git commit -S --signoff (CONTRIBUTING.md lines 62-72).
conventions.testing: In-module #[cfg(test)] mod tests in each languages/*.rs with a parse helper, queries_compile / element / inheritance / defuse tests (java.rs, swift.rs, kotlin.rs, css.rs). Registry tests in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs. Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in(ext, &cwd).
conventions.linting: cargo clippy -- -D warnings (AGENTS.md; issue asks for cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings), cargo fmt --check, workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used and undocumented_unsafe_blocks (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints]); cargo deny check advisories licenses with the 7-day package age gate (CONTRIBUTING.md line 79).
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec and never panic: get_node_text (languages/mod.rs) bounds-checks byte ranges; swift.rs extract_inheritance returns Vec::new() on unexpected kinds. Query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError (parser.rs lines 159-167). Tests use expect() only in test code, which the lint exemption covers.

patterns: Registry: each language is a module under languages/ exporting *_QUERY consts plus optional handlers, wired in languages/mod.rs get_language_info (line 72) and get_ts_language (line 317); lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP (line 12) and supported_languages (line 81) gate detection.

Element capture contract: parser_elements.rs lines 276-293 read capture names 'function', 'func_name', 'method_name', 'class', 'class_name', 'type_name'; other capture names are ignored, so PHP should use class_name rather than Java's interface_name and enum_name.

Inheritance handler signature fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> (ExtractInheritanceHandler); called with the class node from parser_elements.rs line 398-403; Swift's version (swift.rs 49-75) walks children by kind() and is the closest template for PHP's unnamed base_clause and class_interface_clause.

DEFUSE contract: capture prefixes write., read., writeread. classify sites (parser_elements.rs 862-890); a capture is kept only if its node text equals the symbol name; read captures at a byte offset already recorded as a write are dropped.

Java query shape: element, call, reference, import and defuse constants with capture names @function, @class, @method_name, @class_name, @call, @type_ref, @import_path, @write.local, @write.assign, @writeread.update, @read.usage.

Minimal wiring precedent (css): tree-sitter-css in workspace and core Cargo.toml, EXTENSION_MAP entry, pub mod, get_language_info arm with defuse and inheritance None, and get_ts_language arm. css is absent from supported_languages().
Lazy query compilation: parser.rs test near line 1057 asserts that a rust-only parse does not compile every language, so adding PHP does not add startup cost.
Schema: the file-extension JSON schema pattern is derived from EXTENSION_MAP (lang.rs test test_supported_file_ext_pattern_covers_all_extension_map_entries), so adding php there needs no schema edit.

constraints: Maintainer process: the issue states the maintainers are implementing this in-house and external pull requests will be closed; this scout output is for maintainer use, not an external PR.

Scope limits from the issue: no extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type; no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes or namespace alias handling; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no tool handler or schema changes.
Grammar choice: use LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) so inline HTML becomes text nodes and the mixed-file acceptance test can pass with zero ERROR nodes.
The PHP grammar has no 'identifier' node kind (absent from php/src/node-types.json); Java-style (identifier) patterns make Query::new fail, so PHP queries must use (name) and (variable_name).

Dependency gate: tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 was tagged 2026-11-19, about 9 days before this run, so it should pass the 7-day age gate, but the crates.io publish date was not verified; SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK is not allowed by the issue.
Version alignment: the grammar's dev-dependency is tree-sitter 0.27 and the workspace pins tree-sitter 0.27.1, so one tree-sitter version should be in the lock file.
Binary size delta must be measured and stated in the PR description (issue acceptance criteria).
Lint policy: workspace denies unwrap_used, expect_used and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; new handler code must not use unwrap or expect outside tests.
test_coverage: Affected areas are covered by per-language unit tests and registry tests, but PHP has none yet. Java (java.rs) has 6 tests: extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, element query happy path, extract_inheritance, defuse write site. Swift (swift.rs) has queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element_query_matches_class_and_function, extract_inheritance_superclass_and_protocols, extract_inheritance_no_inheritance. Kotlin (kotlin.rs) has about 15 tests covering element, call, import, inheritance and defuse. CSS (css.rs) has rule set, import and empty-file tests. Registry tests: languages/mod.rs test_get_language_info_known, _unknown, test_get_ts_language_known, _unknown and a table-driven test covering tsx, fortran, markdown, css, yaml. lang.rs tests cover the happy path, the edge case, and a test that every EXTENSION_MAP entry matches the schema pattern. parser.rs has a lazy-compilation test. Integration coverage in crates/aptu-coder/tests/integration_tests.rs uses .rs files and unsupported .txt fallbacks; no test in the aptu-coder crate exercises a Swift or CSS file end to end.

approaches.name: A. Java-shaped handler with PHP node kinds (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum_declaration, name captures), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY over variable_name/name, and extract_inheritance that walks base_clause and class_interface_clause by kind. Omit extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type (issue scope). Wire php in languages/mod.rs (get_language_info with LANGUAGE_PHP, get_ts_language), lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages), root and core Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README. Tests in php.rs plus one integration file.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including inheritance and DEFUSE_QUERY
Uses the grammar's real node kinds, verified against node-types.json
Follows the Java and Swift registry shape, so reviewers already know it
Mixed HTML works because LANGUAGE_PHP is used rather than LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY
cons: Inheritance and defuse need hand-written kind walks, not field lookups
Need to confirm the crates.io publish date of tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 clears the 7-day gate without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK
Binary size delta must be measured and stated in the PR description

approaches.name: B. Minimal registry-only port (defuse and inheritance None)
approaches.description: Same php.rs but DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance are set to None in mod.rs and the handler module exports only ELEMENT, CALL and IMPORT queries. Wiring is identical to A (css-style minimal wiring).
pros: Smallest query surface, lowest risk of a query compile failure
Fastest path to a passing cargo test and clippy run
Mirrors the css integration, which also sets defuse and inheritance to None
cons: Fails acceptance criteria: the issue requires extract_inheritance output and the five query constants including DEFUSE_QUERY
analyze_symbol-style def-use results stay empty for PHP variables
Would need a second PR to close the gap, which the maintainers' in-house process makes costly

approaches.name: C. Dual grammar: LANGUAGE_PHP for mixed files, LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for pure .php
approaches.description: Pick the grammar per file by checking for inline HTML (or by extension), using tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for pure PHP and LANGUAGE_PHP otherwise. Requires get_ts_language and get_language_info to accept a per-file grammar choice, and query sets validated against both grammars.
pros: Pure PHP files parse with the smaller PHP-only grammar, which may be faster
Keeps the HTML-template path on the full grammar, so the mixed-file acceptance test still passes
cons: The registry maps one Language per language name (mod.rs get_ts_language), so this changes the shared registry API
Two grammars double the query validation and binary size cost
Unclear benefit: the issue does not ask for a PHP-only path, and the shared element queries would need to work on both trees
Largest blast radius for a single-language addition

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion in the issue (inheritance, all five query constants including DEFUSE_QUERY, mixed HTML) while keeping the change to one handler file plus the same registry wiring Swift and CSS already use. Use (name) and (variable_name) in place of Java's (identifier) patterns, use LANGUAGE_PHP so inline HTML parses, walk base_clause and class_interface_clause by kind because PHP has no superclass or interfaces fields, and keep the crate at tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 after checking its crates.io publish date against the 7-day gate. Approach B is a fallback only if the query work stalls, since it fails the acceptance criteria. Approach C adds shared-registry API churn without a stated need.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Source: tree-sitter-php repo, php/src/node-types.json (node-types) and common/define-grammar.js (rules), read in Step 4.
1. class_declaration: node-types fields are exactly {attributes, body, name}; there is NO superclass or interfaces field. child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces") (the java.rs approach) return None for PHP.
2. Extends clause: define-grammar.js `base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name))`. node-types lists base_clause as a child kind of class_declaration with no field name. Walk: for each child of class_declaration whose kind() == "base_clause", take each named child whose kind() is "name", "qualified_name" or "relative_name" (node-types base_clause children), and push format!("extends {text}").
3. Implements clause: define-grammar.js `class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name))`. Walk: for each child of class_declaration whose kind() == "class_interface_clause", take each named child of kind name | qualified_name | relative_name and push format!("implements {text}").
4. Interfaces: interface_declaration uses the same base_clause for multiple parents, so the same walk yields "extends X" entries. Enums use class_interface_clause for implements (define-grammar.js enum_declaration).
5. Worked case for `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}`: base_clause -> name "Bar" => "extends Bar"; class_interface_clause -> name "A", name "B" => "implements A", "implements B". Result: ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]. A class with neither clause has no base_clause/class_interface_clause children and returns [].
6. Use the bounds-checked get_node_text helper (languages/mod.rs) rather than raw source slicing.
